name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: The reverse Nordic curl is an eccentric quadriceps exercise in which the knees are on a padded surface, the feet are anchored, and the torso leans backward — the opposite direction of the Nordic hamstring curl. The rectus femoris is loaded eccentrically in its stretched position (hip extended, knee flexed) with the bodyweight acting as the resistance. It is one of the few exercises that trains the rectus femoris under hip-extension load with significant knee flexion, complementing the knee-extension exercises commonly used for quad training.

execution.starting_position: Kneel on a padded surface with feet anchored behind (partner or weighted barbell). Start upright on the knees with hips extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Ankle anchoring is required. Use a partner holding the heels or secure the feet under a barbell. Generous knee padding is essential.
steps: Step 1: Kneel upright with feet secured and hips fully extended. Hold the arms across the chest or overhead for progression.
Step 2: Begin to lean backward by allowing the knees to flex — the body leans away from the anchored feet.
Step 3: The quadriceps eccentrically control the backward lean. Lower as far as quad strength allows.
Step 4: Return to the upright kneeling position using the quadriceps concentrically, or use the hands to push off the floor if needed.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you lean back. Inhale as you return to vertical.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hip instead of leaning backward as a whole-body unit from the knees
Dropping too fast in early training, causing excessive DOMS or quad strain
Not using knee padding, making the exercise unpleasant and unsustainable
safety_considerations: Severe DOMS is likely after first exposure — start with 2–3 short-range reps
Avoid if experiencing patellar tendinopathy — consult a clinician
If unable to control even a minimal backward lean, build quad strength with leg extensions before attempting
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lean as far back as quad strength controls. Begin with minimal range (10–20°) and build progressively.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 5-0-1-0 — the eccentric (leaning back) is the entire stimulus; control it maximally
coaching_cues: Lean back as one unit — don't fold at the hip
Quads on — squeeze them to slow the fall
Catch with hands if needed — that's normal for beginners
